table.n: Atlas estimate: spodumene concentrate has no customs code of its own; it is read from HS 253090 ('mineral substances not elsewhere specified'), keeping only the rows from Australia, Zimbabwe, Brazil, Nigeria, Mali and Canada to China, the countries that ship spodumene there: 34% of the tonnage and 72% of the value of the code in 2024. These rows may still hold other minerals. Customs gross weight of concentrate, not lithium content. CEPII BACI HS92 HS 253090 rows to China only, 2024, all transport modes, gross weight; world = sum of all reported flows in the Atlas BACI extract (flows below 1,000 t and 1 M USD omitted)

notes: 2 flows of the lithium chemicals codes (15.1 kt in 2024) are declared under 1,500 USD per tonne, the price of ore or concentrate rather than of a lithium chemical, and are left out of the trade tables: Nigeria to China 8.60 kt at 286 USD/t; Brazil to China 6.48 kt at 1,110 USD/t.
Trade tables and flows are lithium carbonate and hydroxide/oxide (HS 283691, 282520) in gross weight (kt), not lithium content. USGS production is contained lithium (t Li), so units differ.

Spodumene concentrate, the ore concentrate of hard-rock lithium mines, is shown in its own table (Atlas estimate from HS 253090, 5.59 Mt to China in 2024 at 714 USD per tonne on average); it is not added to the chemicals tables, whose tonnes are of another product. Australia declares its spodumene concentrate under this code: its statistics office created the national subheading 25309011 'Lithium concentrates' for it in January 2021 (Australian Bureau of Statistics, Insights into Australian Exports of Lithium, 4 August 2022, CC BY 4.0, https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/insights-australian-exports-lithium).
